About the Host University

Technical University of Liberec (TUL) – Czech Republic

The Technical University of Liberec (TUL) is a prestigious public university established in 1953, located in Liberec, Czech Republic, a member of the European Union and Schengen Area. The university is recognised for its excellence in Engineering, Technology, Architecture, Textile Engineering, Mechatronics, and Applied Sciences. TUL is particularly known for its pioneering research in nanotechnology and nanofibres, including advancements in industrial nanofibre production. The university offers modern laboratories, advanced research facilities, and strong collaboration with European industries. Students benefit from practical learning, innovative research projects, and opportunities for international academic exchange. Located near Germany and Poland, Liberec provides an attractive environment for international students, with relatively affordable living costs. TUL offers selected English-taught programmes and opportunities for students interested in technical innovation, research, and European industry exposure.

Location

About Czech Republic

Czech Republic – A European Hub of Education, Architecture and Engineering

The Czech Republic (Czechia) is a developed Central European country and a member of the European Union and Schengen Area, renowned for its architectural heritage, engineering excellence, and quality education. Its capital, Prague, is famous for Charles Bridge and Prague Castle, while the country is home to Charles University (1348), one of Europe’s oldest universities.

Czechia is renowned for Czech Cubism, represented by the House of the Black Madonna (1912), and the UNESCO-listed Villa Tugendhat (1930). Its engineering achievements include the historic Negrelli Viaduct (1850). Czech scientist Otto Wichterle invented modern soft contact lenses, Jaroslav Heyrovský won the 1959 Nobel Prize in Chemistry, and the word “Robot” originated from Czech literature.
